What is Metabolights?.answer:
MetaboLights is an open access repository for metabolomics studies, including raw experimental data and associated metadata.
To know more:
  1. Methods and resources for omics studies: A curated collection of EMBL-EBI on-demand training.
  2. MetaboLights: Quick tour.
  3. Chemical biology: A curated set of EMBL-EBI online courses.

What training courses are available for.answer:
Metabolomics Training Courses

We offer comprehensive metabolomics training courses ranging from introductory to advanced levels:

- Data analysis workshops
- Practical lab sessions
- Online self-paced modules

sources.title: EMBL-EBI Metabolomics Training
sources.description: Access our comprehensive metabolomics training resources, from introductory courses to advanced workshops in data analysis and interpretation.

How do I access the bioinformatics tools.answer:
Accessing Bioinformatics Tools

You can access our bioinformatics tools through the EMBL-EBI website:

1. Visit [tools.ebi.ac.uk](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/tools)
2. Browse by category or search for specific tools
3. Most tools are freely available
4. Some tools may require registration

sources.title: EMBL-EBI Tools & Resources
sources.description: Browse our comprehensive collection of bioinformatics tools and services.

sources.title: Tools Documentation
sources.description: Learn how to use EMBL-EBI tools effectively with our detailed guides and tutorials.

What is UniProt and how can I use it?.answer:
UniProt Database

UniProt is a comprehensive protein sequence and functional information database providing:

- Detailed protein annotation
- Function descriptions
- Domain structure information
- Post-translational modifications

#How to Use
1. Search by protein name
2. Search by sequence
3. Filter by organism
4. Export data in various formats

sources.title: UniProt: the Universal Protein Resource
sources.description: UniProt is a comprehensive resource for protein sequence and annotation data, created through collaboration between EMBL-EBI, SIB, and PIR.

Can you explain what Ensembl is?.answer: Ensembl is a genome browser that provides visualization and analysis tools for vertebrate genomes. It includes annotation, comparative genomics, variation data, and regulatory features. You can explore genes, transcripts, and genomic regions across multiple species.

sources.title: About Ensembl
sources.description: Ensembl is a genome browser for vertebrate genomes that supports research in comparative genomics, evolution, sequence variation and transcriptional regulation.

How do I submit data to ArrayExpress?.answer: To submit data to ArrayExpress, first prepare your functional genomics data following MIAME guidelines. Use our submission tool Annotare to upload your data files and metadata. We accept various types of functional genomics data, including gene expression, ChIP-seq, and RNA-seq experiments.

sources.title: ArrayExpress Data Submission
sources.description: Learn how to submit your functional genomics data to ArrayExpress using our Annotare submission tool.

What is ChEMBL and how can it help my re.answer: ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties. It contains compound bioactivity data against drug targets, ADMET information, and approved drugs. Researchers use it for drug discovery, chemical biology, and understanding compound-target interactions.

sources.title: ChEMBL Database
sources.description: Access bioactivity data for over 2 million compounds and their interactions with drug targets.

sources.title: ChEMBL Documentation
sources.description: Comprehensive documentation for using the ChEMBL interface and API.

sources.title: ChEMBL Tutorial
sources.description: Get started with ChEMBL through our interactive tutorial.

How do I perform a BLAST search?.answer: To perform a BLAST search on EMBL-EBI's servers, visit our BLAST tool page. Paste your sequence in FASTA format or upload a file, select your database (nucleotide or protein), choose your BLAST program (blastn, blastp, blastx, etc.), adjust optional parameters, and submit. Results will show sequence alignments and statistical significance.

sources.title: BLAST at EMBL-EBI
sources.description: Run BLAST searches against comprehensive sequence databases at EMBL-EBI.

sources.title: BLAST Guide
sources.description: Learn how to effectively use BLAST with our quick tour guide.

sources.title: UniProt BLAST
sources.description: Search protein sequences against UniProt reference proteomes.

What is the European Nucleotide Archive.answer: The European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) is a comprehensive record of nucleotide sequencing information, raw sequencing data, and sequence assembly information. It includes data from whole genome sequencing projects, transcriptome sequencing, and environmental sampling studies.

sources.title: European Nucleotide Archive
sources.description: Access and submit nucleotide sequence data from ENA's comprehensive archive.

sources.title: ENA Quick Tour
sources.description: Get started with ENA through our quick introduction course.

sources.title: ENA Documentation
sources.description: Detailed documentation covering all aspects of using ENA.

How can I access protein structure data.answer: The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) provides access to 3D structures of proteins, nucleic acids, and complex assemblies. You can search by PDB ID, protein name, or organism, view structures in 3D viewers, and download coordinate files in various formats.

sources.title: Protein Data Bank in Europe
sources.description: Explore and analyze 3D structures of biological macromolecules and their complexes.
